title: Pathway-preserving staged swap with oblique shadow and rollback playbook
author: Ayesha Khan
description: Motivation: We observed a class of regressions during staged model swaps that affected long-lived user pathways (multi-request sessions, multi-call chains, and cross-service conversation handoffs). Existing canary and shadow flows validate per-request metrics but lose fidelity on session-level behavioral regressions. This PR introduces a pathway-preserving staged-swap controller plus an "oblique shadow" mode and a compact rollback playbook for operational teams. Design summary: (1) Pathway-preserver: attaches a transient pathway token to user sessions during promotion windows so we can deterministically route subsequent requests from the same logical pathway to the promoted variant for validation without permanently breaking session affinity. (2) Oblique shadow: a controlled, non-blocking shadower that replays a sampled fraction of ongoing session sequences to the candidate model asynchronously, preserving original timing and semantic annotations; responses are recorded but not surfaced to users. (3) Rollback playbook: a lightweight playbook and API to compute impact score from pathway-level deltas (latency tail, loss in intent fidelity, hallucination rate) and execute fast unwind with session handback. Implementation highlights (single-line): adds pathway token lifecycle and lease manager (rollout/pathway_preserver.go), extends orchestrator to support oblique shadow lanes with adaptive sampling (orchestrator/shadow_lane.rs), telemeters pathway traces and delta scoring hooks (telemetry/pathway_emitter.ts), and introduces an integration test harness that replays recorded session traces against old and candidate models to compute cohort-level deltas (tests/integration/pathway_replay_test.py). Backwards compatibility & safety: pathway tokens are optional and scoped; if downstream services don't recognize them, the token is ignored. All new control-plane flags default to off; rollout controller requires explicit enablement by operator via flag --enable-pathway-swap. Operational playbook: included docs/runbooks/pathway-preserve-rollout.md describing step-by-step canary, oblique shadow tuning, smoke thresholds, and automated rollback commands. Why this is different: instead of only looking at per-request aggregates we now validate sequence semantics and preserve user experience across short promotions, enabling earlier detection of regressions that manifest across request chains. Testing & validation: unit tests for token lifecycle, deterministic routing simulation harness, integration replay tests with 3 representative session bundles, and a synthetic smoke run on perf-canary cluster. Deployment plan: feature gated for 2 weeks behind a remote flag; initial rollout to internal tenants then staged to 10% external traffic, monitor pathway delta score for 48 hours, then progressive increase. Metrics to watch: pathway-delta-score, pathway-p99-latency-diff, intent-consistency-drop, model-edge-error-rate. Rollback criteria: automated rollback triggers when pathway-delta-score > 0.15 for two consecutive 30m windows OR intent-consistency-drop > 8% on custodial cohorts. Ops notes: small additional CPU on control plane for pathway lease management; oblique-shadows add async IO but are batched. Security/privacy: replayed requests are redacted according to existing PII pipeline before being stored in replay buckets. Migration notes: replays use anonymized trace ids so A/B experiments are not contaminated. Related work: builds on prior queued shadowing and cohort-aware rollouts but focuses on session-semantics preservation and oblique non-interfering shadow extraction.

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This design looks promising; can you clarify lease duration bounds and what happens if the pathway token expires mid-session?
Ayesha Khan: Lease defaults to 5 minutes and is renewable on activity; the preserver will prefer continuity but falls back to session-sticky routing if lease is missing (documented in runbook).
Priya Sharma: The oblique shadow replay could surface PII in stored traces — ensure redaction executes before write. Add an integration test that asserts no raw PII fields persisted.
Ayesha Khan: Added redaction pipeline hook and a test that asserts persisted trace samples are sanitized. See commit c311d55.
Diego Morales: CI flaked on the new integration test once — observed a timing race in the harness. Can we add a deterministic seed and make sleeps idempotent?
Ayesha Khan: Fixed race by moving to deterministic trace clock in harness and replaced nondeterministic sleeps with channel signaling. Re-ran CI.
ci_checks: integration/pathway-replay: initial run failed (race) -> rerun pass
release_notes: Introduce pathway-preserving staged swap: optional pathway tokens, oblique shadow mode for session replay, pathway-level delta scoring, and an operator playbook for safe promotion and automated rollback. Feature gated behind --enable-pathway-swap.
